findings.label: All three repos are Apache 2.0, so code can be lifted with attribution and a NOTICE.
rakazo's secret model is the closest to a drop-in: request_secret with a reference name and an HTTPS origin, encrypted in Postgres vault_credentials, and list_secrets returns metadata without values.
rakazo injects by proxying the request, not by handing over the value: secret_request takes name, url and method and the backend decrypts and injects.
rakazo states the boundary as a rule: the model has no tool for reading the values, and injecting a credential into a shell command, file or environment variable is deliberately not exposed.
rakazo's computer is a pluggable sandbox provider (E2B, Daytona, Boat, Docker, desktop-fake) behind an AgentHomeStore, with the agent runtime in the API/worker process rather than in the sandbox.
turnstone does per-(user, MCP server) OAuth 2.1 plus PKCE delegation, so each user authorizes a remote MCP server with their own identity instead of sharing one bearer token.
turnstone's per-user OAuth is opt-in per mcp_servers row and dark by default: an install with no oauth_user rows exercises zero new code paths.

turnstone keeps tokens in one encrypted store with a deployment keyring: a Fernet key in config.toml only, with an ordered list for rotation where the first key encrypts new writes and all keys are tried on read.

turnstone's sandbox is kernel-enforced and layered: Landlock for filesystem, network namespace plus seccomp plus an HTTP CONNECT proxy for network, setuid drop for process, and proxy-level secret resolution so keys never sit in sandbox memory.
OpenMausBot delegates secrets to an external password manager: Bitwarden beside 1Password in Settings to Vault, with bw:// references, values read at use and masked wherever text crosses to a bot.

OpenMausBot's computer is the desktop itself: an Electron main process with a CUA host spawning cua-driver over a private socket, plus a WebContentsView pool with per-bot persist partitions driven over CDP.
OpenMausBot's connector is a host agent with its own AppArmor and seccomp profiles rather than a cloud service.

ruledOut.reason: an Electron desktop shell driving a native CUA driver, the largest possible lift
a Python multi-node service with a Fernet keyring, sized for a deployment not a small team

ruledOut.direction: treating any of the three as a connector catalogue
ruledOut.reason: none ships one; all three assume you bring the service
